extracted.intended_audience: aspiring poets, creative writers, critics, and readers of poetry
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on what constitutes a true poet and poetic practice: the mental habits, moral conditions, uses of symbol and language, and the relation of thought and form that make poetry authentic and effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poet_as_representative
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet stands among partial men for the complete man; he represents the common wealth rather than only his private wealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The poet is exemplary and enlarges the reader's sense of humanity. He should be 'more himself than' ordinary men, receiving and imparting more of the soul; his work is valuable because it is representative and makes all men the richer. Antipattern: poets who are merely self-indulgent or narrowly talented without representative insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poet_as_sayer_and_namer
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet is the sayer, the namer, and represents Beauty; he is sovereign in his right to name and announce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: True poetic authority derives from seeing and naming essential relations; the poet gives apt names and rejoices the intellect by detaching and defining. This is not mere rhetorical artifice but a second nature: language-making that issues from deeper perception. Example: poets coined words/imagery that became common; antipattern: those who merely imitate names or fancy conventional epithets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality_of_announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: The sign of the true poet is that he announces that which no man foretold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetry should bring new insight or necessary revelation, not merely pretty sentiment or stylish lyric. Distinguish between talented lyricists who are 'contemporary' and the poet who stands 'out of our low limitations.' Scoring note: value the veracity and novelty of report over mere technical facility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thought_prior_to_form_(metre-making_argument)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not metres, but a metre-making argument that makes a poem — a thought so passionate and alive that it has an architecture of its own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize the originality and organic force of the idea; form should arise from thought. The thought and the form are equal in time, but genesis favors thought. Antipattern: craftsmanship that substitutes polished metre for vital idea ('finish of the verses is primary' in mere talent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced_receptivity_and_capacity_to_impart
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet is the person in whom impressions reach the quick and compel reproduction — a man without impediment who sees and handles that which others dream of and traverses the whole scale of experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate sensitivity and communicative power: be open to impressions but able to translate them. Antipatterns: 'minors' or 'mutes' who cannot report their converse with nature; excessive phlegm or obstruction that dulls the reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use_of_nature_as_picture-language_and_symbol
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature offers all her creatures to the poet as a picture-language; every line or object can be used as an emblem or symbol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ ordinary, even mean, things as potent symbols—small types are often more pungent and memorable. Use nature to certify the supernatural; the poet should see the universal in particulars. Example: household objects, animals, political emblems can all be reworked into poetic meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poet_as_language_archivist_and_inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Poets made all the words; language is fossil poetry and the poet names things after appearance or essence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to coin or re-energize language so that words serve as living symbols. Etymology shows that even dead words were once vivid images. Antipattern: relying only on stale clichés; scoring favors fresh linguistic images that reveal perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagination_as_high_seeing_(intellect_transcended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Imagination is a very high sort of seeing that comes when the intellect is where and what it sees; by abandonment to the nature of things the poet 'overhears' pre-existent melodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate the ability to 'resign' oneself to the aura of forms and accompany their path; practice receptivity (through solitude, attention, moral purity) rather than merely scholarly study. Antipattern: intellectualizing without letting the intellect be 'inebriated' by the fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceiving_multiform_thought_and_metamorphosis
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet perceives that thought is multiform and observes the flowing metamorphosis of forms; within every creature is a force impelling it to ascend into higher forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use processes of transformation (metamorphosis) as poetic method: read natural cycles (birth, growth, gestation) as symbols of spiritual change. Antipattern: static description that ignores inner life and transformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use_forms_according_to_life_not_form
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet uses forms according to the life, and not according to the form; forms should express the life that impels them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match structure and diction to the living force of the idea; avoid formal devices that constrain or falsify the inner vitality. This is 'true science' of poetic use. Antipattern: formalism for its own sake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithful_transcription_of_natural_cadences
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry was all written before time was; the poet overhears primal warblings and attempts to write them down, striving for faithful transcriptions of cadences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for fidelity to the 'music' or cadence inherent in the perceived fact; the best poets lose as few words as possible in transcription. Antipattern: miswriting the poem by substituting mere personal cleverness where a primal cadence was available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Veracity_of_report_over_merely_talented_frolic
rubrics_metrics.description: The value of genius to us is in the veracity of its report; talent may frolic and juggle, genius realizes and adds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate poetry by truthfulness and depth of insight rather than by virtuoso display. The poem's authority rests on being an accurate, illuminating account of experience or idea. Antipattern: ornate but empty verse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbolic_universality_and_fluxionality
rubrics_metrics.description: Symbols are fluxional and vehicular: they convey but must not be fixed into immutable mystical emblems; mysticism mistakes an accidental symbol for a universal one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hold symbols lightly and allow them to serve as transient conveyors of thought; avoid nailing any symbol to permanent dogma. Antipattern: insisting one private symbol be universally paramount (eg. mystic fixation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratic_scope_of_poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetic feeling is universal: hunters, farmers, grooms, and butchers are poets in their susceptibility; all classes use symbols though in different modes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and draw on the common, non-elite sources of imaginative life; do not confine poetic materials to high culture. Antipattern: exclusive elitist taste that thinks poetry belongs only to cultivated classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability_to_elevate_low_and_mean_things
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry can consecrate the low and offensive; small and mean things serve as potent types and can be used to purify or exalt meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use unexpected or coarse material to reveal higher meanings; see defects or deformities as convertible to sacred purpose. Antipattern: shunning low or mundane details as unpoetic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance_of_spurious_stimulants_for_inspiration
rubrics_metrics.description: The sublime vision comes to the pure and simple soul, not to the intoxicated by narcotics; inspiration indebted to opium or wine is counterfeit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor moral and bodily simplicity and natural means of excitation (conversation, music, nature) over drug-induced ecstasy. Example: Milton's distinction — lyric poet may drink wine but epic must 'drink water out of a wooden bowl.' Antipattern: depending on stimulants for poetic power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry_as_emancipation_and_liberation
rubrics_metrics.description: Poets are liberating gods: imagination and tropes emancipate the beholder, offering new worlds and freeing us from prisons of thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A poem should unlock chains and provide a new scene or thought that enlarges the reader's freedom. Measure success by the poem's capacity to reveal and emancipate, not merely to ornament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference_for_transcendental_and_extraordinary_in_books
rubrics_metrics.description: All value in imaginative books resides in their transcendental and extraordinary departures from routine; novelty of witness signals departure and value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prize works that show a genuine break from routine perception, even if they introduce questionable facts; the merit is that they show imaginative departure. Antipattern: overly orthodox, routine, or merely didactic imaginative works.
